title: He built bigger barns…
paragraphs: You can feel it, can’t you?
That quiet lie we whisper to ourselves:
“Just a little more… then I’ll be secure.”

More money.
More savings.
More control.
But what if your “later”… never comes?
Jesus told a story that cuts deeper than comfort.
A man wasn’t wicked in the way we usually define it.

He didn’t steal.
He didn’t kill.
He didn’t oppress.
His land produced abundantly. Overflowing. Beyond expectation.
And suddenly, he had a problem most people pray for.
“What shall I do? I have no place to store my crops.” — Luke 12:17

Blessing became his burden.
Provision became his obsession.
Increase became his identity.
“I will do this: I will tear down my barns and build larger ones…” — Luke 12:18
And then comes the moment no one expects.

No warning.
No countdown.
No second chance.
“But God said to him, ‘Fool! This night your soul is required of you…’” — Luke 12:20
But because he thought he was in control.
You can be financially prepared… and spiritually bankrupt.
You can be building a future… that you will never live to see.
You can be admired by men… and empty before God.
Because money just reveals what you trust.
And this man trusted his barns more than his Creator.

Bank accounts.
Career titles.
Business plans.
Insurance policies.
Backup strategies.
But when they become your peace…
“So is the one who lays up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.” — Luke 12:21
You can have everything the world applauds…
…and still be empty where it matters most.
Because this story doesn’t end in condemnation.
Jesus didn’t just tell this parable to warn you.
He told it to rescue you.
Because every one of us has lived like this rich fool.

We trusted ourselves.
We clung to control.
We built our lives without fully surrendering to God.
And sin always leads to death.
“For the wages of sin is death…” — Romans 6:23
The kind no barn can protect you from.
“…but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.” — Romans 6:23
Jesus stepped into our illusion of control.
Lived the life we couldn’t live.
And rose again to offer what wealth never could:
Meaning your future—if you trust Him—is no longer fragile.
So let me ask you, honestly:
What are you trusting right now?
What are you building your peace on?
What are you afraid to lose?
“Do not lay up for yourselves treasures on earth… but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven…” — Matthew 6:19–20
Of thinking you can secure your life without God.
Because the most dangerous lie is this:
You don’t need to fear that truth.

Lord Jesus, I confess that I have trusted in what I can build more than in You. Forgive me for my pride, my fear, and my need to control. I surrender my life, my future, and everything I have into Your hands. Teach me to be rich toward God. Be my treasure, my peace, and my salvation. Amen.
